title: How this lesson works
text: Before you start · your group ≈ 2 min How this lesson works Slideshow lead Reads each slide aloud and moves the deck forward. Whiteboard scribe Holds the dry erase marker and works problems at the whiteboard. Timekeeper · support Starts each timer and keeps the group on pace. Checker · support Asks "How do we know?" before anyone presses Show answer. Explicit instruction Read it together. Then one person restates it in their own words. Check your understanding Solve alone, compare answers, agree — then press Show answer. Group tasks Start the timer. Everyone contributes before you move on. Exit ticket On your own. title: The asteroid thread

title: What keeps a cart moving?
text: See it → describe it Target R6 What keeps a cart moving? Imagine a cart moving on a very smooth, level track. What happens after the push ends? An ideal low-friction model Without a net horizontal force, the cart keeps a constant velocity. Day 9 · Inertia Antocci Physics · 07 / 31

title: Balanced does not mean stopped
text: See it → describe it Target R6 Balanced does not mean stopped Equal opposite forces give zero net force. The object can be still OR moving at a constant velocity. Read one object’s forces Balanced forces do not tell us the current velocity. Day 9 · Inertia Antocci Physics · 08 / 31

title: After the hand lets go
text: Check your understanding Target R6 After the hand lets go You give a cart a short push on a smooth level track. After your hand loses contact, what happens to the force from your hand? title: The push ended. The motion did not.
text: 2026-XJ · Keep Going · Graphic novel, page 33 The push ended. The motion did not. After Maz releases the cart, it keeps moving. The novel states that the push ended but the motion did not. The hand loses contact, so its force ends. The cart can still move. Real surface and air interactions can change its velocity. Which forces remain after release? How would an ideal zero-net-force case differ? Part 1 · Explain motion after the push · Write your own answer in Work. Fictional story · Original artwork · Day 9

title: Aristotle vs. Galileo
text: Two big ideas ≈ 15 min Aristotle vs. Galileo Aristotle Objects naturally come to rest. Galileo Objects in motion stay in motion — unless something stops them. experiments and idealized motion with less resistance Day 9 · Inertia Antocci Physics · 11 / 31

title: The zero-net-force condition
text: Newton's 1st Law ≈ 15 min In an inertial frame, zero net external force means constant velocity — including rest. Day 9 · Inertia Antocci Physics · 12 / 31

title: Inertia
text: Vocabulary ≈ 15 min Inertia Inertia An object's resistance to a change in its motion. more mass → more inertia Day 9 · Inertia Antocci Physics · 13 / 31

title: Inertia means resisting a change
text: I do · compare the response Target R6 Inertia means resisting a change An object keeps its velocity unless a net force changes it. More mass means more resistance to the same change. Same net force on two carts Illustrative accelerations under the same 4 N net force. Day 9 · Inertia Antocci Physics · 14 / 31

title: Why do real carts slow down?
text: See it → describe it Target R6 Why do real carts slow down? Friction and air resistance can act after a push ends. Those interactions change the velocity. Read one object’s forces A cart moving right can have a net force pointing left. Day 9 · Inertia Antocci Physics · 15 / 31

title: Newton’s first law
text: Explicit instruction Target R6 Newton’s first law In an inertial reference frame, an object at rest stays at rest, and an object in motion keeps the same velocity, unless a nonzero net external force changes that velocity. ΣF = 0 implies a = 0 Day 9 · Inertia Antocci Physics · 16 / 31

title: One coin, two directions
text: 2026-XJ · Keep Going · Graphic novel, page 34 One coin, two directions Mr. Antocci explains that friction had little time to change the coin’s horizontal velocity. Mei explains that gravity made it fall after the card was removed. The supplied story shows little sideways motion and a downward fall. These are story observations, not measurements you collected. Which interaction changes each component of velocity? Does inertia supply another force? Part 2 · Challenge the demonstration explanation · Write your own answer in Work. title: Why does the passenger continue forward?
text: Group discussion ≈ 15 min A car stops suddenly. Why do passengers slide forward? (This is why we wear seatbelts.) Group protocol 1 · Think alone for a minute · 2 · Go around — everyone shares · 3 · Each person records their own reasoning Day 9 · Inertia Antocci Physics · 19 / 31

title: A passenger keeps moving
text: 2026-XJ · Keep Going · Graphic novel, page 35 A passenger keeps moving In a classroom toy model, the car stops while the passenger continues forward. Nadia says no new forward force threw it, and Mei explains that the strap supplies the force that slows it. Use the classroom frame. The car and passenger can change velocity at different times because different interactions act on them. Why does the passenger move forward relative to the car? Which interaction slows the passenger? Part 2 · Compare the interaction explanations · Write your own answer in Work. Fictional story · Original artwork · Day 9

title: Constant velocity is a conditional model
text: Back to 2026-XJ ≈ 13 min Idealization: net external force is zero in an inertial frame. Velocity would stay constant while that condition holds. The actual asteroid still feels gravity. Day 9 · Inertia Antocci Physics · 23 / 31

title: What's pushing it?
text: Back to 2026-XJ ≈ 13 min What's pushing it? Gravity Mostly the Sun — plus weaker pulls from Earth and the Moon. To change its path We need a FORCE. that's the next several days Day 9 · Inertia Antocci Physics · 24 / 31

title: No floor does not mean no force
text: 2026-XJ · Keep Going · Graphic novel, page 36 No floor does not mean no force Mr. Antocci says gravity still acts, especially the Sun’s. Mei says zero net force is a model, not the asteroid’s actual situation. Space lacks the classroom floor, but gravitational interactions remain. Constant velocity is a conditional model. What does zero net force predict? What evidence would challenge that model for the asteroid? Part 3 · Test the limits of the model · Write your own answer in Work. Fictional story · Original artwork · Day 9

title: Inertia and mass
text: Explicit instruction Target R6 Inertia and mass Inertia is resistance to a change in velocity. Mass measures translational inertia. With the same net force, a larger mass changes velocity more slowly. Inertia is a property of the object, not an extra force arrow. Day 9 · Inertia Antocci Physics · 26 / 31

title: Your turn: make sense of a stop
text: Try it yourself Target R6 Your turn: make sense of a stop A cart rolls right, then slows. What does that tell you about its net horizontal force? Solve alone · compare as a group · then check. Velocity over time The rightward velocity is decreasing. Day 9 · Inertia Antocci Physics · 27 / 31

title: Do not draw a “force of motion”
text: Check a common mix-up Target R6 Do not draw a “force of motion” An arrow for velocity describes motion. A force arrow names an interaction with something else. A path through the problem 01 Motion Which way is it moving? 02 Force What object pushes or pulls it? Read one step at a time. Day 9 · Inertia Antocci Physics · 28 / 31
